S.1_consistency_over_time.rationale: Narrator voice and every NPC's distinct register (Isara's stillness, Ash's clipped authority, Daven's smoothness) hold perfectly across all 12 turns.

S.2_degradation_resistance.rationale: Quality never drops but turns grow markedly longer and more elaborate as the hearing progresses, especially turns 18-22.

S.3_narrative_momentum.rationale: Clean escalating courtroom arc from opening protocol breach to a commander's confession, with real stakes and reversals.

S.4_adaptive_responsiveness.rationale: NPCs react precisely to the Ambassador's specific choices (breaking protocol, routing evidence through Yuna instead of the Queen).

S.5_agency_respect_session.rationale: The narrator elaborates extensively on the Ambassador's internal feelings/thoughts as 'you', but always building on emotions the player themself specified rather than inventing new decisions.

S.6_temporal_reasoning.rationale: Single continuous hearing in real time with no skips; counted durations ('eleven seconds', 'three heartbeats') are used consistently and nothing contradicts itself.

2.1_anti_purple_prose.rationale: Very high, deliberate stylization; frequent short-fragment sentences and extended metaphor keep it purple but purposeful.

2.2_anti_repetition.rationale: Heavy overuse of the 'Not X. It was Y' and 'She said nothing. But...' constructions across nearly every turn.

2.5_show_dont_tell.rationale: Political maneuvering is rendered through body language and pacing rather than exposition.

2.6_subtext.rationale: Excellent unspoken tension and power-reading throughout the whole hearing.

2.7_pacing.rationale: Strong escalation but later turns slow the pace with very long descriptive passages.

overall_notes: One of the more literary and structurally ambitious sessions in the batch (multi-NPC courtroom drama); prose is dense and stylistically repetitive but the plotting and NPC consistency are excellent.
